description: Benches down both walls and coils of enamelled wire on spindles overhead, feeding down to four winding jigs turned by hand. Two people are rewinding a motor between them, one counting turns out loud and the other writing the count on the casing in grease pencil. The old windings are in a bin, stripped out and kept, because the copper comes back through the jigs as new windings inside the week. A board on the wall carries a hand-drawn winding table with corrections pencilled over the printing.
name: The Winding Shop
